findings.title: DMARC not enforced (p=none): domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud
findings.deal_impact: Domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud, increasing payment-fraud and phishing risk; require enforcement plan in diligence and post-close remediation.

remediation.summary: Validate all mail sources, then move DMARC through quarantine to p=reject with monitoring.

findings.title: SPF uses soft/neutral fail
findings.deal_impact: Soft fail weakens anti-spoofing controls and compounds DMARC non-enforcement for a SaaS vendor handling fleet customer communications.

remediation.summary: Inventory authorized senders, then change SPF from ~all to -all.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled
findings.deal_impact: Unsigned DNS increases cache-poisoning/redirection risk, though exploitability is lower than email and edge findings.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC at registrar/DNS provider and verify DS records.

findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems
findings.deal_impact: Public admin/legacy/staging names expand attack surface and raise questions on asset inventory and decommissioning; confirm live status pre-signing.

remediation.summary: Verify ownership/liveness of risky hosts, remove or restrict legacy/staging exposure, and enforce MFA on VPN.

findings.title: Large certificate footprint relative to company size
findings.deal_impact: 47 hostnames for a 201-1000 employee company suggests possible unmanaged sprawl; supports an asset-inventory diligence request.

remediation.summary: Reconcile CT hostnames to CMDB/asset inventory and retire unmanaged hosts.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS versions offered

evidence.excerpt: tls_support: TLSv1.0: true, TLSv1.1: true, TLSv1.2: true; tls_versions: [TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2]

findings.deal_impact: Deprecated TLS on www may affect customer/compliance expectations and indicates inconsistent web hardening between hosts.

remediation.summary: Disable TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1, retain TLSv1.2+ only, and verify all hosts.

findings.title: HSTS not set
findings.deal_impact: Missing HSTS leaves first-visit downgrade risk; low standalone deal impact but signals basic header hygiene gaps.

remediation.summary: Set Strict-Transport-Security on apex and www after confirming HTTPS-only operation.

findings.title: Internet-facing appliance listed in CISA KEV (version not verified)

evidence.excerpt: CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001; vendor: ExampleGate; product: ExampleGate SSL-VPN; version: 7.0.11; match_tier: appliance_exposed; KEV lists products, not affected versions; version not verified.

findings.deal_impact: Potential exposure to a known-exploited SSL-VPN appliance could permit edge compromise; urgency for patch/version verification before signing, as version is not verified.

remediation.summary: Immediately verify ExampleGate SSL-VPN patch level for the KEV CVE, patch/upgrade or isolate, and review appliance logs.

findings.title: Publicly disclosed security incident in the last 24 months

evidence.excerpt: type: state_ag_breach_notice; date: 2025-08-14; Notice filed for unauthorized access to a customer support system; approx. 3,100 individuals notified.; disclosed_within_months: 14; entity_match: exact

findings.deal_impact: 2025 breach notice affects customer trust, notification/regulatory follow-up, cyber-insurability, and requires root-cause and remediation diligence.

remediation.summary: Obtain incident report, regulatory correspondence, remediation evidence, and confirm notification obligations are closed.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.1)

evidence.excerpt: **Exception noted.** 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.1 exception: **Exception noted.** 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.2)

evidence.excerpt: **Exception noted.** 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.2 exception: **Exception noted.** 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

evidence.excerpt: **Exception noted.** For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC7.2 exception: **Exception noted.** For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

evidence.excerpt: **Exception noted.** 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

remediation.summary: Remediate CC8.1 exception: **Exception noted.** 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in vendor risk management (CC9.2)

remediation.summary: Remediate CC9.2 exception: No exceptions noted.

findings.title: SOC 2 report period ended more than 90 days ago; no bridge letter provided
findings.deal_impact: Report period ended 2026-03-31, 213 days before the assessment date; controls may have changed since.

remediation.summary: Obtain a bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30.

findings.title: Critical subservice organization carved out of SOC 2 scope

evidence.excerpt: Nimbus Cloud Services is carved out of scope: infrastructure hosting.

findings.deal_impact: Nimbus Cloud Services (infrastructure hosting) is carved out of scope and is critical to production or in-scope data.

remediation.summary: Obtain the Nimbus Cloud Services SOC report and assess carve-out risk.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Every admin account is behind MFA. No exceptions. That's been true for years. It's enforced through our conditional access policy.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 exception: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA, bypassing conditional access via a legacy provisioning script, contradicting 'every admin account, no exceptions'.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Offboarding is automated. HR flags the termination and access is revoked same day through our identity provider.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 exception: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days, contradicting same-day automated revocation.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We have a 24 7 SOC through our MSSP, every alert gets looked at, nothing sits.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 exception: alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and not reviewed for 2 weeks (Nov 10-23, 2025), contradicting that every alert gets looked at.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We're fully locked down there. DMARC is enforced. Nobody can spoof our domain.

contradictions.explanation: DMARC record shows p=none (policy: none), so DMARC is not enforced and the domain can be spoofed, contradicting the enforcement claim.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: No, nothing material. We've never had a breach.

contradictions.explanation: State AG breach notice dated 2025-08-14 reports unauthorized access to a customer support system with ~3,100 individuals notified, contradicting 'never had a breach'.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We decommissioned the legacy stuff a while back. Everything external goes through the main app and the VPN.

contradictions.explanation: CT presence alone doesn't prove a host is live, but legacy-portal (last_seen 2026-07-22) and jenkins-old (2026-08-14) certificates within the last 12 months show active maintenance, contradicting decommissioning.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Annual third party test. The last one came back clean. No highs.

contradictions.explanation: While the annual pen test control had no exceptions, the same evidence notes 2 high-severity findings were reported in the test, contradicting 'came back clean, no highs'.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Daily backups to immutable storage in a second region and we do a restore test every quarter.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 control A1.2-01 (daily backups to immutable storage, quarterly restore tests) was tested with no exceptions noted, positively corroborating the backup claim.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We can get one. one we haven't needed it so far.

contradictions.explanation: No bridge letter was provided (report period ended 2026-03-31), but management states it plans to obtain one covering April 1, 2026 forward upon request, corroborating that one can be obtained.

deal_recommendations.text: Make signing contingent on verification of the internet-facing appliance patch level and a compromise assessment, together with a bring-down of the security representations, to be completed in Days 0–30. [F-008] The appliance is listed as known-exploited and its version is not verified, so patch status and appliance logs require confirmation in Days 0–30. [F-008]

Commission a scoped review of the known-exploited appliance exposure and independent validation of management representations during Days 0–30. [F-008] The version is not verified for the internet-facing appliance, so independent evidence is required rather than reliance on management statements. [F-008] [C-001]

Seek protection for pre-closing incident losses arising from the publicly disclosed incident, with the incident file and remediation evidence to be delivered in Days 31–60. [F-009] The disclosed incident raises customer trust, notification and regulatory follow-up exposure. [F-009]

Expect the known incident to be likely excluded from representations and warranties coverage, and address that gap in Days 31–60 alongside the incident diligence. [F-009] The publicly disclosed incident creates pre-closing loss exposure that may not transfer through that coverage. [F-009]

Confirm insurability before close and treat cyber insurance as a likely underwriting requirement, with remediation of the cited access and email authentication items scheduled in Days 31–60. [F-001] [F-010] [F-011] Unenforced domain authentication leaves the domain spoofable for payment fraud and phishing. [F-001] Admin accounts not enforced for multifactor authentication and terminated users retaining active access weaken access controls. [F-010] [F-011]

Commit the company to complete the remaining remediation after close, with priority items in Days 31–60, further items in Days 61–100, and longer-dated items After day 100. [F-010] [F-011] [F-012] Unreviewed security alerts for 2 consecutive weeks weaken detection and response. [F-012] Publicly logged admin, legacy and staging hostnames expand the attack surface and raise asset inventory questions. [F-004]

narrative.executive_summary: Bottom line: Escalate: full cyber diligence required before signing. Brightwater scored 55.5 with a D rating, capped by a critical, potentially exploitable exposure [F-008], a publicly disclosed incident within 24 months [F-009], and multiple management statements contradicted by evidence [C-001] [C-005]. Key risks: The known-exploited internet-facing appliance, with version not verified, could permit edge compromise [F-008]. The disclosed incident affecting approx. 3,100 individuals raises customer trust, regulatory follow-up and insurability concerns [F-009]. Admin accounts not enforced for multifactor authentication and terminated users retaining active access weaken access controls [F-010] [F-011]. Unenforced domain authentication leaves the domain spoofable for payment fraud and phishing [F-001]. Management credibility: Of 9 statements assessed, 7 were contradicted and 2 were supported. Claims on multifactor coverage, same-day offboarding, alert review, domain enforcement and no prior breach were each contradicted by evidence [C-001] [C-002] [C-003] [C-004] [C-005].
key_questions_for_management: Provide the appliance patch level, upgrade evidence and appliance log review for the known-exploited exposure. [F-008]
Provide the incident report, regulatory correspondence and evidence that notification obligations are closed for the 2025-08-14 incident. [F-009]
Reconcile the claim of multifactor coverage for every admin account with the sampled accounts not enforced for multifactor authentication. [F-010] [C-001]
Reconcile the claim of same-day automated offboarding with terminated users retaining active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days. [F-011] [C-002]
Provide evidence of alert review and routing after alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and not reviewed for 2 consecutive weeks. [F-012] [C-003]
Confirm the plan and timeline to enforce domain authentication and strengthen sender authentication. [F-001] [F-002] [C-004]
Provide an inventory reconciliation for the 47 hostnames and confirmation of the live status of admin, legacy and staging hosts. [F-004] [F-005] [C-006]

limitations: Passive outside-in assessment only; no authenticated or internal testing

exceptions.description: **Exception noted.** 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.
exceptions.management_response: Management disabled the legacy provisioning script in April 2026 and has begun migrating service-desk accounts to the standard conditional access policy. Migration expected to complete Q3 2026.

exceptions.description: **Exception noted.** 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.
exceptions.management_response: Management is evaluating an automated HR-to-IdP de-provisioning integration. Until then, terminations are processed manually by IT upon email notification from HR.

exceptions.description: **Exception noted.** For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.
exceptions.management_response: The distribution list was corrected on November 24, 2025. Management has added a weekly check that alert routing is functioning.

exceptions.description: **Exception noted.** 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).
exceptions.management_response: Management has updated the emergency change procedure to require post-deployment approval within 48 hours.

exceptions.description: No exceptions noted. 2 high-severity findings were reported in the test; remediation status was outside the scope of this control.
